profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite CH1 publishes 180,000 square feet of technical space but no power capacity figure, making its absolute scale for AI workloads impossible to assess from operator specifications.

This facility sits seventh among the seven Illinois data centers that have published power ratings to this site, behind a combined 236 megawatts distributed across six mapped competitors. Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities total, but only this small set disclose their power draw, leaving CoreSite CH1's position within the state's actual infrastructure landscape unclear. The absence of megawattage data is itself the constraint. Without it, square footage alone tells nothing about whether this building can support modern GPU clusters or sustained compute density.

The facility holds security and compliance certifications for SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53, qualifying it for regulated enterprise and government workloads. It also carries PCI DSS and HIPAA certifications, extending eligibility to financial services and healthcare tenants. These certifications address governance and security posture rather than physical capacity for compute density or sustained power delivery.

CoreSite CH1 operates in Chicago as part of a 27-facility portfolio acquired by American Tower in 2021, with the Chicago market entered in 2007. Without published megawattage, colocation pricing, or power purchase agreements disclosed on the operator's specification page, the campus cannot be ranked against peers on the metrics that determine AI infrastructure relevance: available power, power cost, and grid connection to renewable or flexible generation.
